title: Rotating a matrix 90 degrees
summary: Rotate with an index formula, then in place using transpose + reverse.
hints: Work out where one cell goes. Rotating clockwise, the first row becomes the last column: the element at `(r, c)` of an `R x C` matrix ends up at `(c, R-1-r)` of the `C x R` result. Allocate the result (`out` with `C` rows of `R` cells) and assign `out[c][R-1-r] = m[r][c]`.
Counter-clockwise is the mirror image: `(r, c)` goes to `(C-1-c, r)`. Rotating 180 degrees maps `(r, c)` to `(R-1-r, C-1-c)`; you can also just rotate clockwise twice.

In place for a square matrix: rotate clockwise = **transpose, then reverse every row**. Transpose by swapping `m[r][c], m[c][r] = m[c][r], m[r][c]` for `c > r` only (otherwise you swap everything twice and undo it). Then `slices.Reverse(row)` on each row. Go's tuple assignment makes the swap a one-liner.
